rule: waxaana is the focus particle waxaa plus connective -na 'and'. The form itself does not encode a subject person.
source: Morgan Nilsson, Learner's Somali Grammar (2025), University of Gothenburg
source_example: Waxaana gabi ahaan la xiray waddooyinkaas.
source_analysis: waxaana < waxaa + -na; focus particle + connective and
project_execution: Recognize only exact waxaana when it begins the input sentence or an overt following clause/sentence. Do not infer a hidden subject clitic, antecedent, or verb agreement from the connective particle itself.

rule: waxaana belongs to the waxaa/waxa focus-particle family and is not the person-neutral declarative waana, the statement-clitic wuuna/wayna family, or the baa/ayaa connective-subject-focus family.
source: CONN-WAXAA-001 plus existing project focus/statement distinctions

rule: Exact reviewed waxaa-family connective forms may occur sentence-initial as discourse links as well as clause-initial after overt punctuation. Executable recognition may use input start or comma, semicolon, period, question mark, or exclamation mark as the left boundary, but the analyzer must not invent or resolve the preceding discourse antecedent.
source: Morgan Nilsson, Learner's Somali Grammar (2025) sentence-initial Waxaana/Waxayna examples; independently attested sentence-initial Waxaadna examples

rule: waxaana, waxayna, and waxaadna are independently reviewed exact forms. Their promotion does not license waxana, waxaanan, waxaynuna, waxaadinna, or any other predicted waxa/waxaa+clitic+-na form.
source: Exact-form evidence plus project no-paradigm-generation policy

rule: waxayna is an independently documented connective cleft-focus form for third-person feminine singular or third-person plural subjects, matching the reviewed ay subject-clitic ambiguity.
source: R. David Zorc, Somali-English Dictionary; Morgan Nilsson, Learner's Somali Grammar (2025)
source_examples: Waxayna ogaatay in ay Ugaaso bugto oo ay sariirta jiifto.
project_execution: Allow exact waxayna at input-sentence start or after an overt clause/sentence boundary; check only encoded 3sg_f/3pl compatibility against exact reviewed finite morphology. Do not infer an antecedent or generate related forms.

rule: waxaadna is independently attested as connective 'and you ...'; its base waxaad is documented as focus plus second-person subject pronoun/clitic, matching the reviewed aad 2sg/2pl ambiguity.
source: R. David Zorc, English-Somali Finder List for waxaad; exact waxaadna attested repeatedly in Mahmud Muhammad Abduh's Somali Qur'an translation
source_examples: Waxaadna ku cabbaysaan Biyo kulayl badan.
project_execution: Allow exact waxaadna at input-sentence start or after an overt clause/sentence boundary; check only encoded 2sg/2pl compatibility against exact reviewed finite morphology. Do not infer an antecedent or generate related forms.

rule: For exact waxayna/waxaadna, agreement may be judged only when an exact reviewed finite verb is found in the local predicate window. Unknown predicates remain unjudged. waxaana remains person-neutral and never inherits this agreement rule.

Sentence-initial surface position is independently attested for each exact reviewed form; therefore punctuation from a preceding clause is not required inside the input string. The connective meaning may refer to prior discourse that is outside the analyzed string.
